Image size & uploads / FIELD GUIDE

How to convert PNG to JPG, JPG to PNG or WebP correctly

Converting a file is more than changing its name. Choose the format that your destination can actually open.

By Manglo Editorial7 November 20266 min read
THE MANGLO PLAYBOOK / ORIGINAL GUIDE

An application may say “JPG only”, while your phone or design software produces PNG or WebP. The fix is to re-encode the actual image into an accepted format. Editing the letters after the filename dot does not change the underlying image data.

Choose the output format first

FormatUseful forImportant limitation
JPG / JPEGPhotos and broadly compatible uploadsLossy; cannot keep transparent pixels.
PNGSharp text, diagrams, logos, transparent designsPhotographs can become large files.
WebPEfficient images on modern websitesSome external upload portals may not accept it.

Convert an image with Manglo

  1. Open the free image converter.
  2. Choose a JPG, PNG or WebP image from your device.
  3. Select the output format explicitly.
  4. For JPG or WebP, start with moderate-to-high quality and inspect the preview or result.
  5. Download the new file, check its extension and open it once before uploading.

The image conversion happens locally in your browser. The original stays available on your device unless you delete it yourself.

What happens to transparency?

PNG and WebP can contain transparent regions. JPG cannot. When you convert a transparent image to JPG in Manglo, the transparent areas are filled with white. If your graphic must retain a cut-out background, use PNG or WebP and make sure the destination supports it.

Does converting always improve quality or reduce size?

No. Exporting an already blurry JPG as PNG does not restore its original detail. A PNG of a photograph can be larger than the JPG source, and a WebP export may or may not be smaller depending on the image and settings. Keep the original and compare outputs at the same pixel dimensions.

A common mistake

Uploading photo.png after renaming it photo.jpg may still fail because the file remains PNG internally. Use a real converter, then verify the exported result.

Match the destination, not the trend

For a form that explicitly asks for JPEG, choose JPG. For a transparent logo in a design, start with PNG. For a website image where WebP is supported, compare a WebP export. If the main problem is upload size rather than format, use the target-size compressor too.

Format reference: MDN's image file type guide.
